item.title: Yasawa lifts Ranadi Cup
item.description: Yasawa produced a dominant second-half display to defeat their opponents 43-15 and claim the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup title. The final was evenly poised at halftime, with the scores locked at 10-10 after both teams traded points in a physical opening spell.
item.content:encoded:
Yasawa produced a dominant second-half display to defeat their opponents 43-15 and claim the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup title.

The final was evenly poised at halftime, with the scores locked at 10-10 after both teams traded points in a physical opening spell.

Yasawa raised the intensity after the break, taking control through strong defence and clinical finishing. The side ran in a series of tries in the second half while limiting their opponents’ scoring opportunities to pull away on the scoreboard.

Tight head prop and vice captain Tulia Ragadi credited the players for their hard work and teamwork, saying their commitment throughout the match was key to securing the victory.

“This win is a result of the hard work and team spirit shown by every player,” she said.

She also thanked the team’s supporters for standing by the girls throughout the competition.

“We are grateful to everyone who came out to support us. Their encouragement motivated us and played a big part in this victory,” she said.

The win capped off an impressive campaign for Yasawa, who turned a closely fought first half into a convincing 43-15 triumph to lift the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup.

item.title: Mooar urges players to seize pathway
item.description: NEWLY appointed Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar has urged players competing in this year’s Skipper Cup and Deans U18 competition to put their best foot forward, with a place in the professional team potentially waiting for them. With the Skipper Cup kicking off today and the Deans Under-18 elimination rounds also getting underway, Mooar said the Drua coaching staff would be watchi
item.content:encoded:
NEWLY appointed Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar has urged players competing in this year’s Skipper Cup and Deans U18 competition to put their best foot forward, with a place in the professional team potentially waiting for them.

With the Skipper Cup kicking off today and the Deans Under-18 elimination rounds also getting underway, Mooar said the Drua coaching staff would be watching closely for emerging talent.

“My first message will be gone well, good luck, enjoy and have fun, be awesome and also that we’re watching and we’re really inspired by watching and looking for that next Drua player. There’s a pathway here and there’s a jersey with their name on it if they want to put their foot forward and perform. Enjoy,” Mooar said.

Mooar will be in Lautoka today to watch the opening-round Skipper Cup clash between Lautoka and Nadroga.

He said the match would provide an opportunity to see local players competing for their provinces and to experience the atmosphere of the local competition.

“Really looking forward to going to Lautoka to watch Lautoka versus Nadroga in the Skipper’s Cup, opening round, very excited. It’ll be great to be part of that game, part of the day, to see our home ground in action and to see the local players playing hard for their team in the club competition.”

Mooar believes the local competitions are an important part of the pathway towards the Drua and wants the club to work closely with the development structures already in place.

He said the Drua had a major opportunity to build a rugby programme that Fiji could be proud of while developing the next generation of players.

“The opportunity to build a rugby game and rugby product that we are proud of, inspired by, excited by, and is successful for us is huge. I don’t believe there’s any ceiling on where we can take the Drua team to.”

Mooar said getting the Drua programme right must go hand in hand with identifying and developing young talent through competitions such as the Deans Cup and Skipper Cup.

“We nail off making sure that we get right what we’re doing here with the Drua, whilst also working really hard on the pipeline of our talent ID and talent development through the secondary schools Dean’s Cup, the Skipper’s Cup, and embracing that pipeline and pathway and also integrating massively and really tightly with the Fijian Rugby Union through our people, through our players, through our staff, and how we each work together to be able to be equally successful.”

item.title: MGM claims U19 Central Netball Rally title
item.description: MAHATMA Gandhi Memorial High School (MGM) claimed the Fiji Secondary Schools Central Rally Under-19 netball title after defeating Kingdom Ambassador International Fellowship School 19-11 in the final yesterday. MGM produced a composed performance to secure the nineteen-goal victory and book its place at the Fiji Secondary Schools National Netball Championships next month.
item.content:encoded:
MAHATMA Gandhi Memorial High School (MGM) claimed the Fiji Secondary Schools Central Rally Under-19 netball title after defeating Kingdom Ambassador International Fellowship School 19-11 in the final yesterday.

MGM produced a composed performance to secure the nineteen-goal victory and book its place at the Fiji Secondary Schools National Netball Championships next month.

Captain Ateca Buli credited the team’s success to months of hard work and sacrifice.

“The girls have been working since the beginning of this year and they really deserved this win,” Buli said.

“They sacrificed so much, especially with the early morning trainings. We also thank our coaches and parents who have been behind us throughout the journey.”

Buli acknowledged Kingdom Ambassador International Fellowship School for providing a tough challenge in the final, saying both teams had earned their place in the decider.

She said the team was determined to make history by reclaiming the Central Rally Under-19 title for MGM.

“I’m very proud of my girls. We’ve been working so hard for this moment, and all the emotions before the game showed how much this meant to us,” she said.

Winners from the central rallies netball competition; U14-MGM, U15-SGS, U17-SJSS, U19-MGM Open Men’s- YSS, Open Women’s -CMF College

item.title: Tuivuna leads early
item.description: TOMASI Tuivuna currently leads the professional scoreboard after day two of the GM Motors Fiji Golf Classic, which concludes at the Denarau Golf Club today. Tuivuna leads with a gross score of 67, followed by Zoheer Ahmed and Abid Hussain on 69, while Vikrant Chandra is on 71.
item.content:encoded:
TOMASI Tuivuna currently leads the professional scoreboard after day two of the GM Motors Fiji Golf Classic, which concludes at the Denarau Golf Club today.

Tuivuna leads with a gross score of 67, followed by Zoheer Ahmed and Abid Hussain on 69, while Vikrant Chandra is on 71.

In the ladies’ division, Jane Jacobs recorded the best nett score of 65, followed by Merelita McCarthy on 67. Brooke Ball, Sylvia Joe and Anne McMillan all carded 68 nett.

Close to 200 golfers, both young and old, from overseas and Fiji, are competing in the three-day tournament.

Overseas golfer Libby Russell, from the Sunshine Coast, said it was a good time for her to visit Fiji, not only to play golf but also to reconnect with her family.

“I’m loving it, it’s beautiful run, the course is ready.

“For 50 women participants is a good number and the competition is very strong. I’m here because I have never been here before and I have Tonga and Fiji cousins as well,” Russell said.

Neil Sharma, who is based in the USA, was excited to be back in his home country.

item.title: Gold and records for Rainibogi
item.description: Fiji’s Taniela Rainibogi has a gold medal in the men’s 110 kilogram weightlifting at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games. He lifted 170kg in the snatch and 208kg in the clean and jerk – both Commonwealth Games records – for a total lift of 378kg, another Games record.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s Taniela Rainibogi has a gold medal in the men’s 110 kilogram weightlifting at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

He lifted 170kg in the snatch and 208kg in the clean and jerk – both Commonwealth Games records – for a total lift of 378kg, another Games record.

England’s Cyrille Tchatchet II came second, lifting a total of 374 kg, and Canada’s Xavier Lusignan got bronze, lifting 356kg.

Tonga’s Joshua Uikilifi Jr came fourth, 25kg away from a medal.

Vanuatu’s Thomas Wilbur and Samoa’s Jack Opeloge did not finish.

Weightlifting Fiji head coach Henry Elder told FBC it hadn’t been an easy road.

“We have been through this journey – there’s been so many obstacles, so many challenges, so many ups and downs, and God has been faithful up until this very day. And it is to him and him alone that we give glory.”

It’s the Pacific’s second gold and sixth medal in the Glasgow weightlifting program.

Also in weightlifting, David Liti took gold for New Zealand in the men’s +110kg. Liti, while competing under the silver fern, is of Tongan heritage.

Meanwhile, Pacific athletes have been in action in the track and field overnight.

Cook Islands’ Max Teuruaa is competing in the men’s decathlon – a combination of 10 events – which continues into Saturday morning.

He threw a personal best in the decathlon shot put of 11.31 metres, which was 11th of 12 throws.

PNG’s Scholastica Herman ran in the women’s mile, and compatriot Adrine Monagi in the women’s 100m hurdles, but they did not progress further.

In the men’s javelin, PNG’s Lakona Gerega finished 15th, and Tuvalu’s Usufono Eneli 17th of 17 finishers, not qualifying for the final.

In the men’s shot put, Nauru’s Jonathan-Deiwea Detageouwa finished 10th with a season’s best throw of 16.99 metres. Tonga’s Penisimani Taeiloa finished with a ‘no mark’ result, meaning no valid trial was recorded.

The Tonga Tala have now lost four of five games, beaten 55-49 by Malawi.

item.title: NETBALL FIJI REVIVAL I Tourney provides crucial test
item.description: Elite netball returns to the Vodafone Arena from August 3-8 as Netball Fiji hosts the Fiji Invitational Tournament, bringing together four competitive teams for six days. The Fiji Invitational Tournament, supported by the Fiji National Sports Commission, marks a significant milestone in the Crest Fiji Pearls’ journey towards the Oceania World Cup Qualifiers this September and their pursuit of a pl
item.content:encoded:
Elite netball returns to the Vodafone Arena from August 3-8 as Netball Fiji hosts the Fiji Invitational Tournament, bringing together four competitive teams for six days.

The Fiji Invitational Tournament, supported by the Fiji National Sports Commission, marks a significant milestone in the Crest Fiji Pearls’ journey towards the Oceania World Cup Qualifiers this September and their pursuit of a place at the 2027 Netball World Cup in Sydney.

Featuring Fiji Black, Fiji Blue, New South Wales Fiji Davui, and the Auckland Fijians, the Invitational Tournament will provide the national coaching staff with an invaluable opportunity to assess combinations, test game strategies, and evaluate players under competitive pressure.

Head coach Michelle Parsons said the Invitational comes at exactly the right time for the Fiji Pearls as they continue their preparations for the biggest challenge of the year.

“This tournament is an important part of our journey.

“It allows us to see our players perform in competitive match conditions, build combinations, and continue developing the style of netball we want to take into the Oceania Qualifiers.”

Parsons said she has been impressed by the commitment shown throughout the squad.

“The dedication from the players has been outstanding.

“They understand what is at stake, and there’s a genuine hunger to represent Fiji on the world stage.”

“This tournament is another opportunity for them to earn that jersey.”

The Fiji Invitational Tournament not only provides elite competition but also celebrates the growth of netball in Fiji, inspiring the next generation of athletes while strengthening relationships with regional and international partners.

Netball Fiji is encouraging fans, families, and the wider community to come out in numbers and support the Fiji Pearls next week, Monday, August 3 to Thursday, August 6, as they continue their journey towards the 2027 World Cup.

item.title: BA RUGBY NEWS I Late changes provide extra hurdle
item.description: Just as Round One of the Skipper Cup and Subrails Marama Championship approached, Ba’s preparations for their three matches with Suva were thrown into disarray when they heard the game had been brought forward by one day. “The late change, coming on Tuesday, caught us by surprise,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said.
item.content:encoded:
Just as Round One of the Skipper Cup and Subrails Marama Championship approached, Ba’s preparations for their three matches with Suva were thrown into disarray when they heard the game had been brought forward by one day.

“The late change, coming on Tuesday, caught us by surprise,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said.

“It seems there was a miscommunication somewhere along the line about the closure of HFC Bank Stadium this week.”

Not only did the new date mean rushed changes in travel and accommodation, but more importantly it altered team preparations.

“We told the players that these things were out of our control, so don’t let it affect you, just adjust and make do,” Kautoga said.

Some of the players in the NEWWORLD IGA Ba Women’s team were unable to take another day off work at such short notice, so they got left behind.

“They had already arranged to take leave on Friday, but couldn’t get the Thursday off as well when we were travelling around Viti Levu to Suva.”

“It’s a great pity for those players, but they can join us next week when we host Tailevu at 4R Stadium, Govind Park.”

As it happened, the young Ba Women, playing their first-ever match at this level against a side who have been champions multiple times, stood up to be counted.

Playing well-structured rugby, they raced to a 27-7 half-time lead after the opening score from Acelini Tuwai, a brace of tries to Balevuto winger Mereseini Saliucu, plus solo efforts from centre Reapi Savui and Veniasi Lumuka.

Former Fiji Soccer rep Sereana Naweni slotted in a penalty goal midway through the second half to give Ba a handy 30-12 lead, but Suva then showed their experience.

Taking advantage of two yellow cards against Ba within a minute, the large Suva forwards crashed through the Ba defence at regular intervals to narrow the gap.

Ba struggled to hold on, whilst butchering two near-certain tries of their own, and conceded twice in the closing two minutes to give Suva the win after the hooter.

“I’m so proud of these young players,” head coach Sitiveni Kuruvitu said.

“Everything has been stacked against us these past few weeks, but the girls played with such confidence and calmness.”

“To come to Suva, who have long-been a powerhouse in women’s rugby, and dominate some areas of play is a great achievement for our team.”

“We picked up two bonus points and can now look forward to the visit to Ba of Tailevu next week in the knowledge that we can compete at this level.”

The Fiji Pine U20’s suffered a similar heartbreak, conceding the winning try to their hosts after the hooter as Suva edged the game 24-21.

Suva had led 19-0 after half an hour, but the Penaia Cokomata-coached side found their rhythm and picked up three converted tries to lead 21-19 after 80 minutes.

Suva centre Joji Lutumailagi came strong when his side needed him and dived over for the winning score.

In the main Skipper Cup match, Vinod Patel Ba made a vast improvement over the last two encounters with Suva, but fell just short 26-28 when the last gasp conversion attempt sailed a metre wide.

Suva had jumped to an early 15-0 lead but Ba stayed close.

Tries in the final stages to replacement fullback Viliame Cama and wing Solo Druku brought Ba to the verge of their first-ever win over the Capitals, but Joseva Nokelevu couldn’t quite curl in his conversion.

So, Suva have started their campaigns with narrow wins in all three categories, but the efforts from the Ba teams will surely be recognised and built on.

Next Saturday, we can expect a bumper crowd for Tailevu’s visit to 4R Stadium, Govind Park. Tickets are $10 for adults, and $5 for children aged 5-11.

item.title: Eastern Zone Netball Rally ends on a high
item.description: The 2026 Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Rally concluded at Nasau Park in Levuka, with Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association vice president Joshua Qalo commending the standard of competition and the collective effort that delivered another successful championship. Qalo said the tournament produced exciting contests across all grades, particularly in the Under-15, U17 and U19 divisions.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Rally concluded at Nasau Park in Levuka, with Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association vice president Joshua Qalo commending the standard of competition and the collective effort that delivered another successful championship.

Qalo said the tournament produced exciting contests across all grades, particularly in the Under-15, U17 and U19 divisions.

“Leading up to the finals, it was an exciting performance by schools, particularly in the U19s, U15s and U17s, which were closely contested,” he said.

He also praised emerging schools that made their mark during the two-day competition.

“Wainibuka has shown they are going to be a team to watch at the Fiji Secondary Schools National Championships,” Qalo said.

He added that Vunimono High School (VHS) had also impressed throughout the tournament, proving they should not be overlooked heading into the national competition.

As the rally came to an end, Qalo thanked everyone who contributed behind the scenes.

“We’re thankful to the host schools, the Fiji Police Force, our umpires, scorers, stakeholders and everyone who contributed to making the Eastern Secondary Schools competition a success,” he said.

On the court, Adi Cakobau School (ACS) claimed the U14 title with a 19-9 victory over Lelean Memorial School (LMS). Wainibuka Secondary School (WBK) edged ACS 23-21 to win the U15 grade, while VHS defeated ACS 19-12 in the U17 final.

ACS bounced back to secure the U19 title after defeating Levuka Public School 35-21 before adding the Open Girls crown with a 15-9 win over WBK. VHS wrapped up the rally by edging Noco Secondary School 11-10 to claim the Open Men’s title.

Attention now turns to the Fiji Secondary Schools National Championships, where the Eastern Division’s top teams will look to build on their strong performances.
